headline: Epidemiologic Notes and Reports Fatal Diphtheria -- Wisconsin
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: A 9-year-old Wisconsin girl who had not been immunized died of diphtheria on July 14, 1982, the first diphtheria death reported in Wisconsin since 1968.

headline: Mumps Outbreaks on University Campuses -- Illinois, Wisconsin, South Dakota
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Marquette University in Milwaukee reported 178 cases of mumps between February 4 and May 14, 1987, the largest of the campus outbreaks described in this report.

headline: Treating measles: the appropriateness of admission to a Wisconsin children's hospital.
source: American Journal of Public Health (via PubMed Central)
blurb: This study reviewed the charts of 634 patients with a measles diagnosis who were treated at a Wisconsin children's hospital between August 1989 and April 1990, during a measles outbreak in the metropolitan area.

headline: On the Role of Different Age Groups and Pertussis Vaccines During the 2012 Outbreak in Wisconsin
source: Open Forum Infectious Diseases (via PubMed Central)
blurb: This study of Wisconsin's 2012 whooping cough outbreak counted 7,481 reported cases from late 2011 through early 2013, and 75% of them were in children under age 17.

headline: Public Health Actions to Control Measles Among Afghan Evacuees During Operation Allies Welcome — United States, September–November 2021
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: On September 4, 2021, CDC was told of a suspected measles case in a person evacuated from Afghanistan to Fort McCoy, Wisconsin, and 22 of the 47 confirmed cases among evacuees were in Wisconsin.

headline: DHS Monitoring Significant Increase in Pertussis (Whooping Cough), Urges Vaccination to Prevent Severe Symptoms
blurb: The Wisconsin Department of Health Services said it had received reports of 625 confirmed whooping cough cases as of September 13, 2024, compared with 51 cases reported in 2023.

headline: DHS Confirms First Cases of Measles in Wisconsin This Year
blurb: The Wisconsin Department of Health Services and Oconto County Public Health confirmed nine measles cases in Oconto County, all exposed to a common source during travel out of state.
